title: Finlytics POC: hosting recommendation and deployment deltas
summary: Notes and recommendation for Finlytics POC. Customer requirement: low-latency, audited data handling for financial signals; model size mid-parameter (13B) with 8k context for some workflows. This doc compares hosted / dedicated / private options and proposes a hybrid Dedicated + Private fallback with phased rollouts and observable SLOs.
customer_context: Customer: Finlytics (mid-market fintech, regulatory in EU/UK)
Primary workload: real-time signal enrichment and compliance summarization for trade desk (short prompts) + batch overnight report generation (long context)
Security: must demonstrate data residency in EU region and KMS integration for secrets; SOC2 plus extra audit trail on inference inputs for regulatory review
Traffic profile: baseline 180 req/s during market hours (09:00-16:30 CET), peak spikes to 900 req/s for batch triggers and market events; batch jobs: 1200 long-context tokens/run overnight
Latency target: p95 <= 75ms for enrichment endpoints; batch can tolerate minutes
Budget guidance: cap initial monthly inference spend equivalent to $60k hosted; customer open to reserved commitment for price predictability
recommendation: Primary: Redwood Dedicated (EU region) pinned to 13B quantized runtime with autoscale for market spikes. Secondary (compliance-sensitive flows): Private VPC deployment for audit-only endpoints and KMS-controlled keys. Global fallback policy: route to hosted in non-sensitive, low-cost tier for best-effort continuity.
recommendation_rationale: Dedicated meets throughput + latency SLOs with predictable cost and isolation for Finlytics production traffic
Private VPC required for specific audited endpoints to meet customer's compliance team requirements and KMS/HSM integration
Hosted remains useful for non-sensitive development/experimentation and as a fallback if Dedicated capacity is exhausted
Hybrid approach minimizes up-front private infra while satisfying regulatory constraints and predictable billing
deployment_options_matrix: Hosted (EU): pros = fastest onboarding, no infra to manage; cons = auditability gaps, higher unit $ without committed discounts; risk = fails compliance gating for audited endpoints

Dedicated (EU reserved pool): pros = predictable throughput, SLA-backed latency + quotas, cost savings at commit; cons = requires capacity planning and warm-up strategies for large model context windows
Private VPC (customer-managed networking): pros = full audit trail, KMS/HSM control, air-gapped option; cons = ops burden, longer lead time (2-6 weeks) for setup and validation
Hybrid (Recommended): Dedicated for primary traffic, Private for auditable paths, Hosted for dev/fallback. Tradeoff: increased operational complexity but aligns with Finlytics risk posture
capacity_and_cost_estimates: Assumptions: 13B model quantized to 4-bit equivalent throughput; average tokens per request (enrichment) = 120; batch jobs average 6k tokens
Baseline (Hosted) cost estimate: $0.0008 per token -> projected monthly = $72k for current traffic profile
Dedicated (reserved monthly commit 60% of baseline usage) estimate: ~35% lower unit cost -> projected monthly commit spend = $46k with headroom for autoscale bursts

Private initial setup: one-time infra + integration estimate = $18k engineering + 2 weeks validation; steady-state infra cost ~similar to Dedicated but with integration overhead and optional support premium
Operational note: enabling prefix/KV caching for enrichment endpoints reduces token utilization by estimated 22% (saves ~8-10% on total cost under current profile)
rollout_plan: Week 0-1: finalize SLOs, sign reserved commitment for Dedicated EU pool (target capacity = baseline * 1.4)
Week 2-3: deploy model artifact to Dedicated, run synthetic load tests (p50/p95/p99 latency capture), enable KV caching on enrichment endpoints
Week 4: pilot routing 10% of production traffic to Dedicated from hosted, collect error/latency/cost metrics
Week 5-6: enable Private VPC for audited endpoints (subset of API paths) and cutover audit workflow with KMS integration; run compliance checklist
Week 7: increase Dedicated traffic to 75%, fallback rules set to Hosted for capacity exhaustion, begin runbook/doc handover to Finlytics SRE
fallback_and_graceful_degradation: Policy: if Dedicated p95 latency > 150ms or queue depth > 80% for 2 consecutive minutes, route non-audited traffic to Hosted fallback within 3s
Audited endpoints: never fail open to Hosted. If Private unavailable, degrade to read-only cached responses and notify compliance owners
Autoscale: prefer vertical-burst (additional capacity in Dedicated) for sub-5min load events; for sustained >10min spikes, trigger reserved burst pool or temporary routing to Hosted with cost alert
risk_register: Risk: Dedicated warm-start for 8k context long requests causes occasional p95 spikes during batch start. Mitigation: scheduled warm-up job 10m before market open; validate KV prefix warming
Risk: Compliance team rejects Hosted -> Private sway. Mitigation: early SOC2 artifacts + audit trail demo during week 3 workshop
Risk: Cost overruns in first month due to underestimation of token counts. Mitigation: conservative estimate + cost cap alerting and throttles
Risk: KMS integration with Private keys delays cutover. Mitigation: parallel integration testing with test keys and runbook for key rotation
workshop_observations: Customer product lead pushed for maximum locality to reduce latency for European desks
Compliance strongly insisted on auditability for quoted-response flows used in client reporting
SRE noted that their team prefers Dedicated because they lack bandwidth to manage full Private infra in parallel
Dev teams want a shared dev-hosted environment for feature iteration; recommended separate sandbox project in Hosted
open_questions: Which endpoints must be auditable end-to-end vs. which can be best-effort? (Action: product + compliance to label endpoints by Fri)
Customer willingness to commit to a 6-12 month Dedicated reserve for better unit pricing? (Action: commercial to propose 3-tier commitment options)
Are there any EU-specific HSM requirements that force on-prem Private instead of VPC? (Action: security to confirm with Finlytics security contact)
Can Finlytics accept degraded cached responses for audited flows if Private is temporarily unavailable? (Action: compliance decision needed)
Expected batch job concurrency window overnight — confirm exact cron triggers and concurrency (Action: infra to capture logs for two-week sample)
next_steps: Schedule technical design review with Finlytics SRE + Redwood infra (target: 2025-02-20)
Commercial: draft Dedicated commitment options and pricing delta for 3 / 6 / 12 months
Solutions Eng: prepare KV caching config and synthetic load scripts for the 13B quantized runtime
Compliance: assemble minimal audit artifact pack (SAML logs, KMS flow diagram, access controls) for review in week 3
Follow up workshop: session to label endpoints as auditable vs non-auditable and finalize fallback tolerance
